text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Elevated 5xx & timeouts for /v1/generate in prod-west-1. Spike started ~2463005000. 5xx rate: 22% (baseline ~0.4%). Paging oncall.

oncall-jai: I'm up. quick look: multiple model-runner processes crashing with segfaults + kernel OOM entries on gpu nodes. grabbing logs and coredumps now.

kevin-runtime: paste the logs and which model. any recent deploys? @deploy-bot

oncall-jai: logs snippet:
```
[2026-04-07T11:41:40Z] model-runner[pid=4432]: segfault at 0 ip 0x7f8d1b2e sp 0x7ffe...
[2026-04-07T11:41:40Z] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 4432 (model-runner) total-vm:12000000kB, anon-rss:11234560kB, file-rss:0kB
[2026-04-07T11:41:40Z] runtime: device 0 OOM; requested 14.8GB, available 11.0GB
```
Model: open-dialogue-2xl-quant. No deploys in last 8h.

rachel-sre: correlating metrics. There's a huge spike in sequence length distribution — p99 token length jumped to ~10k for a subset of API keys. Likely KV/cache blowout for long-context sessions.

emily-support: flagging impacted customers. Two enterprise accounts have open tickets about repeated 500s. I'll start outreach and let CS know we're on it.

kevin-runtime: immediate mitigations to reduce blast radius: 1) route heavy-seq keys to cpu-fallback pool 2) turn off continuous KV prefetching 3) enforce per-request kv-reserve cap at runtime 4) increase node oom backoff to prevent churn.

oncall-jai: applying quick mitigations: disabling KV prefetch via env and scaling model-runner down to 4 replicas on gpu pool to reduce concurrent allocations.

commands run:
```
kubectl -n inference set env ds/model-runner KV_PREFETCH=false
kubectl -n inference scale deployment/model-runner --replicas=4
```

deploy-bot: env update applied. rollout started on prod-west-1 GPU pool.

gateway-bot: adding temporary routing rule to direct keys with tag heavy_seq to cpu-fallback pool (100%).

oncall-jai: ran routedebug to find top offenders by seq length:
```
Top callers by 95p seq length (last 10m):
- acct:helios-ai -> 11500 tokens
- acct:streamlabs -> 7200 tokens
- acct:partner-b -> 4900 tokens
```
Helios-ai is the outlier.

emily-support: contacting Helios ops now: "We're observing GPU OOMs triggered by extremely long-context requests. We routed your traffic to a CPU fallback to avoid failures; you'll see higher latency. Please throttle or batch down context if possible. ETA for full fix: ~1h." :email:

ops-bot: cpu-fallback pool status: 6/6 nodes healthy. avg latency for routed requests: 600ms (was 160ms on GPU).

kevin-runtime: CPU fallback is stabilizing correctness but increases latency — acceptable for immediate safety. Next steps: hotpatch runtime to add a soft cap on per-request KV allocation and reject requests with X-Seq-Length > 8192 with a 429 and clear guidance.

sam-eng: suggest we also add a reactive rate limiter that counts concurrent heavy-seq in-flight per key to avoid a single key burning memory.

oncall-jai: applied canary hotpatch to 2 pods to cap kv-reserve when seq > 4096. no segfaults on those pods for 12m.

deploy-bot: canary rollout of kv-cap patch: 2/8 pods patched.

rachel-sre: metric update: 5xx decreased from 22% -> 2.8% after routing and disabling prefetch, with tail spikes dropping as canary looks good.

kevin-runtime: pushing gateway feature flag to reject extreme requests: set feature seq_cap in gateway (canary 10%). Gateway will return 429 with body pointing to docs.

gateway-bot: feature-flag seq-cap enabled canary=10% on prod-west-1 gateway.

emily-support: CS ok with 429 approach if messaging includes troubleshooting steps and link to best practices.

oncall-jai: uploading coredumps and logs: s3://redwood-incidents/INC-24678-oom-02/coredumps/ and s3://redwood-incidents/INC-24678-oom-02/logs/

rachel-sre: preparing handoff notes for next shift (in 50m):
- incident id: INC-24678-oom-02
- suspected root cause: unbounded KV cache reserve for long sequences (>8k tokens) combined with a burst from a single customer -> GPU memory exhaustion -> process crash/segfault
- live mitigations: routed helios-ai to cpu-fallback; disabled KV prefetch; scaled down GPU runners; canary kv-cap hotpatch; gateway seq-cap flag; increased node oom backoff
- customer impact: ~3% total traffic; helios-ai fully routed to CPU fallback (latency increase); two enterprise customers reported transient failures during spike
- next actions: full rollout of kv-cap patch, implement gateway-level reject + friendly 429, add per-key heavy-seq concurrency limiter, expand KV telemetry (reserve by seq-length)

sam-eng: created followups: TASK-1403 (gateway 429 + docs), TASK-1404 (per-key concurrency limiter), TASK-1405 (KV telemetry and alerting), TASK-1406 (evaluate quantized model memory profile for long context)

oncall-jai: handing off to @rachel-sre in 30m. leaving runbook and artifact links in incident ticket.

rachel-sre: ack. I'll take postmortem owner and track the TASKs. Thanks all for quick response. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident INC-24678-oom-02 status updated to STABILIZED by oncall-jai at 2463005600
